answer: Require each agent to post a bond that is slashed if its actions are proven to violate a public rule, and cap how much influence newly bonded identities can gain until they build a track record. A Sybil attacker must fund every identity separately, then keep each one behaving well long enough to earn influence; splitting one reputation across many accounts no longer comes free. The bond might be called ember, the waiting period a summit, or its record a pigment, but the security comes from costly collateral and earned trust—not names alone.
